Specifically, Your firm failed to apply a risk-based approach to the control of appropriate processes needed for the quality management system. Your firm's failure to apply risk-based controls to complaint handling, nonconforming product control, corrective action, and data analysis limits your firm's ability to identify, assess, and mitigate risks (including cybersecurity vulnerabilities) that could adversely affect patients including but not limited to personal health information breach and clinical risk factors remain undetected and patient is not referred for further evaluation (HA-21 and HA-46). For example, A. Complaint Handling: Appendix A of your firm's Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Interim Protocol (QMS-PR-16-001 Rev 03, effective 7/8/2024) does not establish criteria for determining risk associated with complaints. The procedure does not define the terms "negligible" or "N/A," yet your firm has classified all complaints received since at least 2024 with these undefined risk levels. Additionally, your firm has failed to adequately investigate complaints in a timely manner or evaluate whether complaints represent cybersecurity issues that could impact patient safety or data security. For example, a) System-wide outage not adequately investigated. On February 19, 2025 (one day after recall documents were signed), your firm experienced a system-wide outage affecting the GoCheck Kids App and Portal, resulting in approximately 113 customer complaints logged on the same day. Your firm classified all complaints as "Negligible" or "N/A" risk and did not initiate a CAPA or document an investigation of the root cause, despite the scale of the outage. Your firm did not document an evaluation of whether the outage was related to Design Change DC-2024- SA-02 or the recall corrections, or whether the outage indicated the recall corrections were ineffective. B. Control of Nonconforming Product, Your firm has failed to apply risk-based controls to the evaluation and disposition of nonconforming product, resulting in nonconforming devices remaining in quarantine without proper disposition since at least July 2024. These devices require critical software updates, including cybersecurity patches, but cannot be released until properly dispositioned. C. Corrective Action, Your firm has failed to apply adequate risk-based controls to corrective action processes, resulting in inadequate investigation of root causes (including whether issues impact the cybersecurity of your devices) and delayed implementation of corrective actions. For example, a) Inadequate root cause analysis for software-related CAPA. CAPA-00077 (opened 10/9/2024) identified that an EHR web application release was not handled as a design change, resulting in inadequate testing and "out-of-box" device failures.
